message.content: {"caption":"Flow diagram of a reasoner proposing and solving tasks, with separate rewards feeding a joint update.","description":"A process diagram places a purple rounded box labeled “Absolute Zero Reasoner” on the left. A solid pink path labeled “PROPOSE” rises from the reasoner and points right into a green “Construct & Estimate” box, marked with a Python logo. Beneath it, a white outlined “Task Types” box lists Abduction, Deduction, and Induction as equation-like patterns using O, P, I, and dotted unknown placeholders: the legible patterns include “? = P (I)” for Deduction and “O = ? (I)” for Induction. The legend defines P as Program, I as Input, and O as Output. A solid dark connector runs from the right side of the Task Types box upward to a junction on the Construct & Estimate output line; a separate solid dark arrow labeled “Self-play” points left from the Task Types area toward the reasoner. A solid blue path labeled “SOLVE” descends from the reasoner and points right into a green “Verify” box, also marked with a Python logo. The Python logos indicate that Python is used in the construction/estimation and verification stages. On the right, a dashed reward connection runs right from the Construct & Estimate junction to a peach “Learnability Reward” box, whose dashed arrow points down to a dark “Joint Update” box. A dashed connection runs right from Verify to a peach “Accuracy Reward” box, whose dashed arrow points up to Joint Update. The legend identifies solid arrows as model input/output and dashed arrows as model reward.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
